fanoutqa_030539.t: North America :: History :: Pre-Columbian era :: part 02 :: chunk_0006
fanoutqa_030539.x:
North America :: History :: Pre-Columbian era :: part 02 :: chunk_0006
The first recorded European references to North America are in [Norse sagas](/wiki/Vinland_sagas "Vinland sagas") where it is referred to as [Vinland](/wiki/Vinland "Vinland").[[56]](#cite_note-60) The earliest verifiable instance of [pre-Columbian trans-oceanic contact](/wiki/Pre-Columbian_trans-oceanic_contact "Pre-Columbian trans-oceanic contact") by any European culture with the North America mainland has been dated to around 1000 CE.[[57]](#cite_note-61) [The site](/wiki/L%27Anse_aux_Meadows#Norse_site_(c._1000) "L'Anse aux Meadows"), situated at the northernmost extent of the island named [Newfoundland](/wiki/Newfoundland "Newfoundland"), has provided unmistakable evidence of [Norse](/wiki/Norsemen "Norsemen") settlement.[[58]](#cite_note-62) Norse explorer [Leif Erikson](/wiki/Leif_Erikson "Leif Erikson") (c. 970–1020 CE) is thought to have visited the area.[[e]](#cite_note-64) Erikson was the first European to make landfall on the continent (excluding Greenland).[[60]](#cite_note-65)[[61]](#cite_note-66)

The Mayan culture was still present in [southern Mexico](/wiki/Yucatan_Peninsula "Yucatan Peninsula") and Guatemala when the Spanish [conquistadors](/wiki/Conquistador "Conquistador") arrived, but political dominance in the area had shifted to the [Aztec Empire](/wiki/Aztec_Empire "Aztec Empire"), whose capital city [Tenochtitlan](/wiki/Tenochtitlan "Tenochtitlan") was located further north in the [Valley of Mexico](/wiki/Valley_of_Mexico "Valley of Mexico"). The Aztecs were conquered in 1521 by [Hernán Cortés](/wiki/Hern%C3%A1n_Cort%C3%A9s "Hernán Cortés").[[62]](#cite_note-Grunberg-67)

[The Walt Disney Company](/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company") commissioned the series after the success of Disney Channel's previous music-based franchises, such as the made-for-television film *[High School Musical](/wiki/High_School_Musical "High School Musical")* (2006). *Hannah Montana* was produced by [It's a Laugh Productions](/wiki/It%27s_a_Laugh_Productions "It's a Laugh Productions") in association with Poryes's production company, and premiered on Disney Channel on March 24, 2006. A [concert film](/wiki/Concert_film "Concert film"), *[Hannah Montana & Miley Cyrus: Best of Both Worlds Concert](/wiki/Hannah_Montana_%26_Miley_Cyrus:_Best_of_Both_Worlds_Concert "Hannah Montana & Miley Cyrus: Best of Both Worlds Concert")*, in which Miley Cyrus performs as Hannah Montana and herself, was released in 2008. The following year, the feature film *[Hannah Montana: The Movie](/wiki/Hannah_Montana:_The_Movie "Hannah Montana: The Movie")* was released. The series concluded on January 16, 2011, as a result of Cyrus's growing popularity and music career, and her desire to move into more mature acting roles. Cyrus executive-produced and appeared in the *[Hannah Montana 20th Anniversary Special](/wiki/Hannah_Montana_20th_Anniversary_Special "Hannah Montana 20th Anniversary Special")*, which was released on [Disney+](/wiki/Disney%2B "Disney+") on March 24, 2026 to commemorate the 20th anniversary of the series.

*Hannah Montana* is one of Disney Channel's most commercially successful franchises. It received consistently high viewership in the United States on cable television and influenced the development of merchandise, [soundtrack albums](/wiki/Soundtrack_album "Soundtrack album"), and [concert tours](/wiki/Concert_tour "Concert tour"). Saturn is a [gas giant](/wiki/Gas_giant "Gas giant"), composed predominantly of [hydrogen](/wiki/Hydrogen "Hydrogen") and [helium](/wiki/Helium "Helium"), and lacks a definite [surface](/wiki/Planetary_surface "Planetary surface").[[31]](#cite_note-melosh2011-33) Saturn has a "diffuse core", extending 60% of the way to the planet's surface, composed of an indeterminate gradient of rock and ice toward the center.[[32]](#cite_note-34) Saturn is the only planet of the Solar System that is less dense than water—about 30% less.[[33]](#cite_note-preserve-35) The average [specific density](/wiki/Relative_density "Relative density") of the planet is 0.69 g/cm3 due to its atmosphere. Capps") served non-consecutive terms; he is counted chronologically as both the ninth and sixteenth mayor. The longest term was that of [Pete Wilson](/wiki/Pete_Wilson "Pete Wilson"), who served for eleven years over three terms prior to the establishment of successive term limits. The shortest term, not counting interim or acting mayors, was that of [George P. Tebbetts](/wiki/George_P._Tebbetts "George P. Tebbetts"), who served for less than two months before the position of mayor was abolished due to the bankruptcy of the city. [Percy J. Benbough](/wiki/Percy_J._Benbough "Percy J. Benbough") is the only mayor to have died in office. Two women have been elected mayor: [Maureen O'Connor](/wiki/Maureen_O%27Connor_(California_politician) "Maureen O'Connor (California politician)") and [Susan Golding](/wiki/Susan_Golding "Susan Golding") consecutively. [John F. Forward Sr.](/wiki/John_F._Forward_Sr. "John F. Forward Sr.") and [John F. Forward Jr.](/wiki/John_F._Forward_Jr. "John F. Forward Jr.") are the only father and son to have both served as mayor. [Todd Gloria](/wiki/Todd_Gloria "Todd Gloria") is the first mayor of color, with Filipino, Latino, and Native American heritage. Gloria is also the first elected mayor to be openly gay.[[26]](#cite_note-Los_Angeles_Times-26)

This list includes people who served as acting mayor or interim mayor due to a vacancy in the office of the mayor, but who were not officially elected or appointed as mayor. The acting and interim mayors are not included in the count of mayoralties.

In 2007, the [Football Association of Ireland](/wiki/Football_Association_of_Ireland "Football Association of Ireland") and [Scottish Football Association](/wiki/Scottish_Football_Association "Scottish Football Association") proposed the expansion of the tournament, which was later confirmed by the UEFA Executive Committee in September 2008.[[65]](#cite_note-65)[[66]](#cite_note-66) Out of the 54 member associations of UEFA, only three, including [England](/wiki/The_Football_Association "The Football Association") and [Germany](/wiki/German_Football_Association "German Football Association"), opposed the expansion.[[67]](#cite_note-platini-annoyed-67) On 28 May 2010, UEFA announced that [UEFA Euro 2016](/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2016 "UEFA Euro 2016") would be hosted by France. France beat bids of Turkey (7–6 in voting in the second voting round) and Italy, which had the fewest votes in the first voting round.[[68]](#cite_note-68) Euro 2016 was the first to have 24 teams in the finals.[[69]](#cite_note-69) This was the third time France have hosted the competition. After he was recalled in 1801 by the new president [Thomas Jefferson](/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson"), Federalist leaders in Massachusetts arranged for Adams's election to the United States Senate in 1802. However, Adams broke with the Party over foreign policy and was denied re-election. In 1817, President [James Monroe](/wiki/James_Monroe "James Monroe") selected Adams as his secretary of state. * Between April 1848 and February 1849, [Joseph Dalton Hooker](/wiki/Joseph_Dalton_Hooker "Joseph Dalton Hooker") explored parts of northern Sikkim and eastern Nepal, mainly to collect plants and study the distribution of Himalayan flora. He was based in Darjeeling, and made repeated excursions in the river valleys and into the foothills of Kangchenjunga up to an elevation of 4,760 m (15,620 ft).[[35]](#cite_note-35)
* In spring 1855, the [German](/wiki/Germans "Germans") explorer [Hermann von Schlagintweit](/wiki/Hermann_von_Schlagintweit "Hermann von Schlagintweit") travelled to Darjeeling but was not allowed to proceed further north due to the [Third Nepal–Tibet War](/wiki/Third_Nepal%E2%80%93Tibet_War "Third Nepal–Tibet War"). In May, he explored the [Singalila Ridge](/wiki/Singalila_Ridge "Singalila Ridge") up to the peak of [Tonglo](/wiki/Tonglu,_West_Bengal "Tonglu, West Bengal") for a meteorological survey.[[34]](#cite_note-Schlagintweit1871-34)
* In 1879, [Sarat Chandra Das](/wiki/Sarat_Chandra_Das "Sarat Chandra Das") and Lama Ugyen-gyatso crossed into Tibet west of "Kanchanjinga" via eastern Nepal and the [Tashilhunpo Monastery](/wiki/Tashilhunpo_Monastery "Tashilhunpo Monastery") en route to [Lhasa](/wiki/Lhasa_(prefecture-level_city) "Lhasa (prefecture-level city)"). They returned along the same route in 1881.[[36]](#cite_note-Das1902-36)
* In 1883, a party of [William Woodman Graham](/wiki/William_Woodman_Graham "William Woodman Graham") together with two [Swiss](/wiki/Swiss_people "Swiss people") mountaineers climbed in the area of Kangchenjunga. They were the first who ascended [Kabru](/wiki/Kabru "Kabru") within 9.1–12.2 m (30–40 ft) below the summit. They crossed the Kang La pass and climbed a peak of nearly 5,800 m (19,000 ft) from which they examined Jannu. They concluded it was too late in the year for an attempt and returned once again to Darjeeling

India has not had a national language since its [independence in 1947](/wiki/Indian_Independence_Act_1947 "Indian Independence Act 1947"). However, Rule 1976 (As Amended, 1987) of the [Constitution of India](/wiki/Constitution_of_India "Constitution of India"), mandates English as the "Official Languages" required "for Official Purpose of the Union." Business in the Indian parliament is transacted in either Hindi or in English. English is allowed for official purposes such as parliamentary proceedings, judiciary, communications between the [Central Government](/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India") and a State Government.

States within India have the liberty and powers to select their own official language(s) through legislation. In addition to the two Official Languages, the constitution recognises 22 regional languages, named in a specific list as "[Scheduled Languages](/wiki/Languages_with_official_status_in_India "Languages with official status in India")". (Hindi is but English is not.) India's Constitution includes provisions detailing the languages used for the official purposes of the union, the languages used for the official purposes of each state and union territory and the languages used for communication between the union and the states.

[Hindi](/wiki/Hindi "Hindi") is the most widely spoken language, mostly prevalent in the northern parts of India. The Indian census takes the widest possible definition of "Hindi" as a broad variety of the "[Hindi Belt](/wiki/Hindi_Belt "Hindi Belt")".[[3]](#cite_note-4) According to [2001 Census](/wiki/2001_Census_of_India "2001 Census of India"), 53.6% of the Indian population declared that they speak Hindi as either their first or second language, in which 41% of them have declared it as their native language.[[4]](#cite_note-5)[[5]](#cite_note-6)[[6]](#cite_note-7) 12% of Indians declared that they can speak [English](/wiki
